cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Approve the Cover Story
cards.instruction: Get someone to endorse an explanation that protects the plan, reputation, or people involved.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: If the caretaker asks, we were checking the props cupboard for extra seating. Can you stick to that?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll tell him we borrowed his key to get the chairs.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Stools. Chairs don't fit. And don't volunteer the key before he's asked about it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He lent it to me. He'll expect me to say how we used it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then say you lent it on to me. I'll explain the seating check. Please don't improvise any furniture.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 seeks agreement on a protective account. A3 corrects B2's chairs detail and disclosure order; B4's key responsibility makes A5 reassign explanation while retaining the coached seating story.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's chairs are corrected to stools in A3. B4 explains why the key cannot be omitted, so A5 incorporates its transfer and offers to answer about the cupboard.

relationship.evidence: B2 wants to provide a usable account and B4 owes the caretaker an explanation of a lent key. That obligation makes B more than a passive accomplice.

heightening.evidence: A5 takes over the difficult explanation because B4 has made the earlier omission strategy untenable, while still policing B's furniture claim.

specificity.evidence: A1 caretaker, props cupboard and seating establish the story being rehearsed; B4 explains the key's custody.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's furniture instruction recalls B2's concrete error. It is a final direction to the helper, though it has a small comic flourish.
